pages.headline: Cabinet approves NDC 3.0 for 2031-35
pages.what: The Cabinet approved India's third NDC under the Paris Agreement for 2031-35: 47 per cent lower emissions intensity of GDP from 2005, 60 per cent non-fossil capacity and an additional 3.5-4.0 billion tonnes carbon sink.
key: Emissions intensity: 47 per cent cut from 2005
Non-fossil: 60 per cent of cumulative capacity
Status: 52.57 per cent non-fossil capacity by February 2026
pages.static: NDCs are submitted every five years to the UNFCCC; India's net-zero goal is 2070.

pages.headline: CMS COP15 adds 40 species to Appendices
pages.what: CMS COP15 at Campo Grande, Brazil, added 40 species, subspecies and populations to its Appendices, 20 of them to Appendix I, and launched a Global Initiative on Taking of Migratory Species.
key: Theme: Connecting Nature to Sustain All Life
pages.static: CMS (Bonn Convention, 1979) is a UNEP-linked treaty; India is a Party.
pages.angle: Trap: swapping Appendix I and II.
pages.remember: App I: extinction danger; App II: cooperation.

pages.headline: Migratory species update: decline widening
pages.what: The interim update found 49 per cent of CMS-listed migratory populations declining and 24 per cent threatened. The Scimitar-horned Oryx moved to Endangered and the Saiga to Near Threatened.
key: 24 per cent at risk of extinction (was 22)
Saiga Antelope: Endangered to Near Threatened
Threats: habitat loss, H5N1, overexploitation, bycatch
pages.static: IUCN categories run Extinct, Extinct in the Wild, Critically Endangered, Endangered, Vulnerable, Near Threatened.
pages.remember: Oryx EW to EN; Saiga EN to NT.

pages.headline: India files 7th CBD national report
pages.what: The report tracks 23 national biodiversity targets, shows tree and forest cover at 25.17 per cent and 24.1 million hectares under restoration. Land degradation affects 29.77 per cent of the area.
key: Forest and tree cover 25.17 per cent
24.1 mha restored vs Bonn Challenge pledge of 26 mha
pages.static: The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (2022) has 23 targets for 2030, including 30 by 30.
pages.angle: Trap: saying the Bonn pledge is already met.

pages.headline: India's first Nagoya Protocol report
pages.what: India filed its first national report on the Nagoya Protocol. India issued 12,830 ABS approvals and published 3,556 Internationally Recognised Certificates of Compliance, about 60 per cent of the global total.
key: Needs prior informed consent and mutually agreed terms
pages.static: Section 39 of the Biological Diversity Act deals with designation of repositories.

pages.headline: WMO: Earth's energy imbalance at 65-year peak
pages.what: The WMO report added Earth's energy imbalance as a key indicator and found it at a 65-year peak. 2025 was 2nd or 3rd warmest at about 1.43 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial.
key: Released on World Meteorological Day, 23 March
EEI included for the first time
pages.static: WMO is a specialised UN agency headquartered at Geneva.

pages.headline: National repository for deep-sea fauna named
pages.what: The Bhavasagara Referral Centre of CMLRE, Kochi became the National Repository for Deep-Sea Fauna under Section 39 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002.
key: CMLRE under Ministry of Earth Sciences
pages.static: Section 39 allows the Centre to designate repositories for biological material.

pages.headline: SC notices sand mining in Chambal
pages.what: The Supreme Court took suo motu cognisance of illegal sand mining at the National Chambal Sanctuary, which protects the gharial, red-crowned roof turtle and Ganges river dolphin.
key: Suo motu cognisance by the Supreme Court
Tri-junction of MP, UP and Rajasthan
Also protects red-crowned roof turtle, Ganges river dolphin
pages.static: The gharial is Critically Endangered and in Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

pages.headline: Two GIB chicks hatch; captive stock reaches 70
pages.what: Two new chicks hatched at the breeding centre in Rajasthan, taking captive birds to 70, in the fourth year of the programme.
key: Centre at Desert National Park, Jaisalmer (2019)
pages.static: The GIB is Rajasthan's state bird and the focus of a Supreme Court case on power lines.

pages.headline: India now has 98 Ramsar sites
pages.what: India's 7th National Report to the CBD records 98 Ramsar sites as of 2026, up from 26 in 2014. India ranks first in Asia and third globally for Ramsar sites, and the report lists wetland expansion among its achievements.
key: 98 Ramsar sites as of 2026, up from 26 in 2014
Cited in India's 7th National Report to the CBD
Ramsar Convention adopted in 1971 in Ramsar, Iran
pages.static: The Montreux Record lists Ramsar sites where ecological character is changing or likely to change; Keoladeo and Loktak have been on it.

pages.headline: Hope Island Olive Ridley eggs protected
pages.what: Almost 20,000 Olive Ridley eggs were safeguarded on Hope Island in Kakinada Bay by the Wildlife Management Authority and the Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary.
key: Hope Island, Kakinada Bay, Andhra Pradesh
Wildlife Management Authority with Coringa WLS
pages.static: Mass nesting (arribada) of Olive Ridleys happens in Odisha's Gahirmatha and Rushikulya.

pages.headline: NBWL clears Pobitora boundary rationalisation
pages.what: The National Board for Wildlife approved Assam's proposal to rationalise the boundary of Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary.
key: Proposal from Assam to rationalise boundary
pages.static: Projects near protected areas need NBWL clearance under the Wildlife (Protection) Act.

pages.headline: Draft EIA amendment to cut State-level delays
pages.what: The draft creates Standing bodies in each State to step in when SEIAA or SEAC are non-functional or slow, for a maximum of one year.
key: SAEIA replaces SEIAA for max one year
SCEIA replaces SEAC for max one year
pages.static: EIA is mandatory for listed projects; the 2006 Notification classifies them as Category A and B.

pages.headline: First National Highways Green Cover Index
pages.what: NHAI and ISRO's NRSC released the first NH-GCI covering about 30,000 km of national highways in 24 States.
pages.static: NRSC, Hyderabad, runs Bhuvan, India's geoportal.

pages.headline: NPC named Environment Audit Designated Agency
pages.what: NPC signed an agreement with MoEFCC to act as Environment Audit Designated Agency under the Environment Audit Rules, 2025. It will manage the audit framework, set eligibility criteria, register auditors and monitor performance.
key: Sets eligibility criteria and registers auditors
NPC set up in 1958; under DPIIT, Commerce Ministry
Member of the Asian Productivity Organisation, Tokyo
pages.static: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is the umbrella law for environmental regulation in India.
pages.angle: Trap: placing NPC under the environment ministry.
pages.remember: NPC audits the environment but belongs to Commerce.

pages.headline: Draft ELV rules with recycled steel target
pages.what: The draft rules set a 10 per cent recycled steel requirement and bring insurers into the scrap process; comments until 26 May 2026.
pages.static: Vehicle scrapping is governed by ELV rules under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
pages.remember: Ten per cent steel, comments 26 May.

pages.headline: Green ammonia and methanol standards notified
pages.what: MNRE set maximum emissions for green ammonia at 0.38 and green methanol at 0.44 kg CO2e per kg, with hydrogen at 2.
key: Green hydrogen: at most 2 kg CO2e per kg H2
pages.static: Green hydrogen is made by electrolysis using renewable electricity.
pages.angle: Trap: assigning the hydrogen number to ammonia.

pages.headline: ISA marks Foundation Day
pages.what: The ISA marked its Foundation Day. It aggregates demand to reduce costs for LDCs and SIDS and was envisioned as an alternative OPEC.
pages.static: The ISA is headquartered at Gurugram.

pages.headline: UN water report: 2.1 billion lack safe drinking water
pages.what: The UN World Water Development Report 2026, tied to the 'Water and Gender' theme, says 2.1 billion people still lack safely managed drinking water. Women and girls are the main collectors, spending over 250 million hours daily.
key: Tied to World Water Day 2026 theme 'Water and Gender'
2.1 billion lack safely managed drinking water
Women and girls collect most household water
pages.static: SDG 6 aims at clean water and sanitation for all by 2030.
pages.remember: Water and Gender: 2.1 billion without safe water.

pages.headline: International Day of Forests 2026: Forests and Economies
pages.what: International Day of Forests, observed on 21 March, carried the 2026 theme 'Forests and Economies', stressing that conservation must go with economic development. Forests supply timber and non-timber produce such as bamboo, honey, gums and tendu leaves.
key: Proclaimed by UNGA in 2012; first observed 2013
Forests give timber and non-timber forest produce
World Water Day follows on 22 March
pages.static: The Forest Rights Act, 2006 recognises forest-dwellers' rights over minor forest produce.
pages.angle: Trap: merging it with World Water Day.

pages.headline: Water Day conclave releases censuses
pages.what: The conclave released the 7th Minor Irrigation Census, the 2nd Census of Water Bodies, the first Census of Springs and the National Water Data Policy 2026.
pages.static: Water is a State subject (Entry 17, State List), with inter-State rivers under Entry 56, Union List.

pages.headline: Delhi tests TiO2 anti-pollution coatings
pages.what: Delhi partnered with IIT Madras to test titanium dioxide photocatalytic coatings that use sunlight to break down NO2 and volatile organic compounds. They limit secondary PM and ozone but do not remove primary PM2.5 and PM10.
key: Photocatalytic TiO2 coatings on roads and surfaces
Break down NO2 and VOCs using sunlight
Limit secondary PM and ground-level ozone
Concern: nitrate runoff into the Yamuna
pages.static: A photocatalyst speeds a chemical reaction under light without being consumed.
pages.angle: Trap: claiming they clear primary PM.
pages.remember: TiO2: sunlight cleans gases, not primary dust.

pages.headline: ISRO traces Dharali flood to ice-patch collapse
pages.what: ISRO concluded the Dharali flood was caused by an ice patch collapse in the Srikanta Glacier's nivation zone, not a cloudburst or GLOF.
key: ICIMOD: HKH melt rate doubled since 2000
pages.static: Nodal agencies: MoJS, CWC; NDMA runs the National GLOF Risk Mitigation Programme.

pages.headline: M.C. Mehta PIL formally closed
pages.what: The Supreme Court closed the 1985 PIL. It recognised absolute liability and applied the public trust doctrine.
pages.static: Article 21 and 48A/51A(g) anchor environmental jurisprudence.

pages.headline: CSE: extreme weather on 99 per cent of days in 2025
pages.what: The CSE report said extreme weather struck on 99 per cent of days in 2025 with 4,419 deaths, and only 15 per cent of people live near a continuous air monitor.
key: Extreme events on 99 per cent of days in 2025
15 per cent within 10 km of a monitor
40 per cent of tiger territory overlaps 60 million people
pages.static: CSE also publishes Down To Earth magazine.
